  <script type="application/ld+json">
  {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "FAQPage",
    "mainEntity": [
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "What is the most important composition technique for beginners?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Rule of thirds, no contest. You do not need any special gear — just turn on the grid overlay on your phone camera and start placing your subject along those lines instead of in the center. You will see a difference in your very first shoot. Get comfortable with thirds before you even think about the other techniques."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Can I combine multiple composition techniques in one photo?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Yes, and honestly the best photos almost always do. A landscape with a leading line pulling your eye toward a subject placed on a thirds intersection, with foreground elements creating depth — that is three techniques working together. The trick is not to force it. Start with one technique until it becomes automatic, then start layering."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Do composition rules apply to social media photos or just professional photography?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "They matter more for social media, if anything. Your image is competing for attention in a feed where people are scrolling fast, and a well-composed photo stops the scroll because it looks balanced and intentional. The same thirds, leading lines, and negative space I use for client work are exactly what I use for my own Instagram posts."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "How long does it take to develop good composition instincts?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Faster than you might think for the basics, longer than you would hope for true instinct. I noticed real improvement within the first few weeks of deliberately practicing thirds placement. But making compositional decisions without thinking about them took me closer to a year of regular shooting. The thing that helped most was reviewing my photos after each shoot and asking which compositions worked and why."
        }
      }
    ]
  }
